derivedFrom.assumption: basic pay scaled by the source file's projectedRaiseToNextYearPct of 3.6%, rounded to the cent, clamped where a row would exceed its grade's ceiling: O-7 to O-10 at the Executive Schedule Level II ceiling, every other grade at the Level V ceiling. Special and incentive pay rates are NOT scaled — they are fixed statutory amounts carried forward as published. IRS limits are held at the prior value and marked not-official rather than projected. Nothing here is transcribed from a publisher; this file is a projection and every figure in it should be replaced by transcription when the real tables publish.

figureTime._comment: v57 §3.7/§3.8 — TWO CLOCKS PER FIGURE, both read out of the captures in cowork/reference/dfas-2026/ and neither taken from any directive. effectiveFrom/To is the RATE clock: when this amount took effect. authorityExpiresOn is the AUTHORITY clock: when the legal power to pay this entitlement at all lapses unless Congress renews it, from the DFAS Duration of Authority table (page updated April 7, 2026). They are independent — a rate can be perfectly current while its authority is weeks from lapsing, which is exactly the situation below. authorityPermanent is NEVER a default: absence of an expiry means notEstablished, not permanence.

payTable._authority: Basic pay does not appear on the Duration of Authority table — it is permanent statutory pay, not a bonus or incentive requiring renewal. But ABSENCE IS NOT PERMANENCE (§3.8b): nothing captured states that affirmatively, so the authority clock is NOT ESTABLISHED rather than permanent.
